e: Belgium and Rwanda renew relations after an 18-month break, following a meeting hosted by Qatar in Doha.

A court in the Netherlands sentences Eugene N., a Rwandan-born Dutch citizen, to life imprisonment for genocide and war crimes over his role in the massacre of 3,000 Tutsis in Mbazi during the Rwandan genocide in 1994.

Prosecutors in Germany arrest a German–Rwandan national in Hesse on suspicion of complicity in the 1994 Rwandan genocide, including 25 counts of murder while serving as an assistant to the mayor of Kayove during the killings.
The United States imposes sanctions on FDLR commander Gustave Kubwayo over his involvement in the ongoing DRC–Rwanda conflict.
L'Archive, a memorial in Paris commemorating the victims of the Rwandan genocide, is inaugurated by President Kagame and French President Emmanuel Macron.

Rwanda loses its lawsuit against the United Kingdom before the Permanent Court of Arbitration, which rejects Rwanda's claim seeking £60 million in compensation from the termination of the Rwanda asylum plan.
Rwanda signs a nuclear cooperation agreement with Russia.
Rwanda closes the Goma-Gisenyi border crossing with the DRC amid the 2026 Ituri Province Ebola epidemic.
The United States imposes sanctions on multiple unidentified senior Rwandan officials on charges of "fueling instability" in the eastern DRC.

The U.S. Department of State imposes sanctions on the Rwandan Defence Force and multiple senior military officials, over support for M23 rebels in eastern DRC and violating the 2025 DRC–Rwanda peace agreement.
Two spectators at the Tour du Rwanda are killed after being struck by an out-of-control vehicle in Gabiro.
Rwanda files a lawsuit against the United Kingdom in the Permanent Court of Arbitration, seeking £50 million ($68.8 million) in damages from the improper termination of the Rwanda asylum plan.
